Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the sample.

Quick summary of options and our suggested path:
1) Single invoice + distribution CSV (recommended): Redwood issues one invoice that contains full line detail with a machine-readable distribution file (entity_id, line_id, net_amount, vat_amount, cost_center). Your ERP ingests the CSV and posts per-entity. This preserves one invoice number for your payments team while enabling apportionment in your ledger.
2) Multiple invoices (one invoice per legal entity): Redwood issues four invoices, each with the correct VAT stamping and remit instructions. This is clearer for auditor trails but requires payment coordination across multiple invoices.

From an operations perspective we can deliver option (1) within 3 business days once you provide: a) the entity mapping (VAT IDs, legal names, remit accounts) and b) preferred cost center codes. I've attached a short template (entity_mapping_template.csv) to collect these fields.

If you prefer option (2) we need to confirm invoice numbering scheme and whether you need separate invoice PDFs or consolidated PDF with cover sheet per entity.

Next steps: if you can return the completed template today we will scope the export and confirm the ETA for delivery.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ping. Operational notes below:

- We can support option (1) (single invoice + distribution file). For audit clarity we should: include line-level entity tags on the invoice PDF and produce a signed distribution CSV with a reference column to the invoice line number.
- VAT treatment: if the entities have different VAT regimes we must reflect VAT per line on the PDF. That means the PDF will contain per-line VAT amounts and totals by VAT ID. The distribution CSV should repeat VAT_ID and VAT_amount per line.
- Multiple invoices (option 2): We'll reserve a contiguous invoice number block (e.g., RBW-2027-042-A..D) so payments referencing a single PO can still be reconciled. This increases bookkeeping overhead but is acceptable if the customer prefers.
- Invoice numbering / remit: If we issue multiple invoices, each invoice PDF will carry entity-specific remit instructions. For single-invoice + CSV, the PDF remit remains the consolidated remit; the CSV will include target remit_account fields for your ERP to split payments. Some banks require separate payment instructions per entity, so verify with the customer whether their payments team can split to multiple accounts from a single invoice.

I've attached our internal remit playbook that lists mandatory fields and sample CSV format (remit_instructions_playbook.pdf).

Suggested next steps: Dylan to confirm with Brightline whether they want per-line VAT on the PDF. If yes, we proceed with option (1) and populate the CSV. If no, consider option (2).

-Kim
